Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 22736 of 2023

Applicant :- Chandrakesh Vishwakarma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Chandra Prakash Misra,Ravi Kumar Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sanjay Kumar Mishra
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Chandra Prakash Misra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha,
learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
87 of 2023, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 376 IPC, Police Station Ahirouli Bazar, District Kushinagar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and two others on 26.2.2023 through an application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C dated 23.1.2023 and according to the FIR, informant/victim was a major and married lady aged about 30 years and applicant committed rape with her on 6.11.2022 and thereafter on 24.11.2023 on the enticement of the applicant victim had taken entire jewellery at bus station but applicant did not arrive there and when on 26.11.2022 she went at the house of the applicant then he refused to recognized her and when she demand her money and jewellery then he alongwith his family members started abusing her and also made assault upon her.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and FIR of the present case was lodged on the basis of the application under section 156 (3) Cr.P.C and even application under section 156 (3) Cr.P.C was lodged after about 2 months of the alleged incident and this fact clearly suggests that entire allegation of rape against the applicant is totally false and baseless.

He further submitted that admittedly victim is a major and married lady and from the statements of the victim recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. it reflects that it is a case of consensual relationship and victim in her both the statements admitted that she stayed alongwith the applicant for seven months and it appears thereafter some dispute arose and she made allegation of rape against him.

5. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that victim is a major and married lady and in her both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., she admitted this fact that she stayed with the applicant for seven months and FIR of the present case was lodged through an application under section 156 (3) Cr.P.C. and even application u/s 156(3) was moved after two months.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Victim i.e. informant of the case is a married and major lady aged about 30 years and she in her statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. stated that she had stayed with the applicant for seven months, therefore, it appears that it is a case of consensual relationship.
8. Further, FIR of the present case was lodged through an application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C and even application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C was lodged after two months of the alleged incident.
9. Therefore, considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, as discussed above, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant-Chandrakesh Vishwakarma be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
